problem_text:
A logistics company needs to schedule 5 delivery routes through 5 distribution centers.

Each route consists of a sequence of processing stages represented as pairs (Center, Duration),
where each pair specifies the distribution center where the stage must occur and the time required for processing.
The order of pairs indicates the required sequence in which the stages must be completed.

Route details:
* R1 requires the sequence: (DC4, 3) → (DC2, 4) → (DC5, 3) → (DC1, 8) → (DC3, 6)
* R2 requires the sequence: (DC4, 4) → (DC5, 8) → (DC2, 4) → (DC3, 10) → (DC1, 1)
* R3 requires the sequence: (DC4, 6) → (DC1, 1) → (DC5, 3) → (DC3, 4) → (DC2, 10)
* R4 requires the sequence: (DC3, 7) → (DC1, 8) → (DC5, 1) → (DC2, 9) → (DC4, 9)
* R5 requires the sequence: (DC4, 4) → (DC5, 6) → (DC2, 5) → (DC3, 1) → (DC1, 1)

Each processing stage must run continuously once it begins and cannot be interrupted,
and each distribution center can only handle one processing stage at a time.
The objective is to determine the processing sequence of all stages across the distribution centers
so that the total completion time of all delivery routes is minimized.
